<!--

The newly added added recording_list functionality for philips_js https://github.com/home-assistant/core/commit/01c49ba0e4250d9e50c73a74714308916bc0badb has a bug, which did not occured while developing.
It was missed to add a scenario in which the TV has the right API and has the needed functionality.
Neverless for some TV the recordings_list is not available if the TV is off or in StandBy.

This PR adds a check prior accessing the data to prevent an error.

review_comments: Just add a check before thks line with return false.

if api.recordings_list is None:
  return false

You mean instead of:  `return not isinstance(api.recordings_list, type(None))` ?
(I think Github does not indicate the line exactly again)

If I would add it to _check_for_recording_entry, the function will wrongly return false for all and indicate, that "no" recording is available or no recording is running instead of the more correct "unknown".

Just thought about it again.
The three-state idea in my last comment will turn the entities to _unknown_ everytime the TV decides to be in a deep-sleep and outputs None. So it will jump between _unknown_ and _on/off_ in the worst case.

My PRs implementation will just update the state to _on/off_ if there is an update by the TV and just the initial startup-state will be _unknown_.
I see little benefit with three state.. Just have it go false.
